findings.title: Renumbering RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 breaks the documented exit-code contract
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was 4 and is now changed to 3, while 4 is reused for the new FEATURE_DISABLED constant. The user guide (and this PR's own docs) explicitly instructs automation to rely solely on the command's exit code, so any pipeline or external caller that treated exit code 4 as 'recreate required' will now receive 3 for that case and 4 for 'feature disabled' — a silent behavioural break. Introducing FEATURE_DISABLED as a new value (e.g. 5) and leaving recreate at 4 would have preserved the contract. Also verify that all internal consumers reference the constant rather than a hard-coded 4, since a literal would now be misinterpreted.

findings.title: New exit code 4 and renumbered exit code 3 are never asserted
findings.body: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the printed error string and does not assert that the command exits with FEATURE_DISABLED (4). Likewise testWrongVersions only asserts the error message and never checks the recreate exit code, which this PR just changed from 4 to 3. Since the documented contract is that consumers rely only on the exit code, the two values that matter most for automation are untested; a regression in either the feature-disabled path or the recreate path (e.g. a wrong picocli.exit value) would not be caught.

findings.title: Caution says the operator fails without rolling-updates, contradicting the default-strategy test
findings.body: The new [CAUTION] states the feature rolling-updates must be enabled or the Operator will fail. But UpgradeTest#createInitialDeployment returns without enabling the feature whenever updateStrategy is null (the default '<not set>' strategy), and both testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount expect that default deployment to succeed (recreate on image change, rolling on config change). So the operator demonstrably does not fail in the default case. The caution should be scoped to using the new update.strategy field rather than implying every deployment needs the preview feature, otherwise operators are misled into enabling a preview flag unnecessarily.
